question: Under the Energy Efficiency Directive and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364, data centres are subject to mandatory Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) reporting. However, data collection does not ensure the preservation of resources. EU law fails to set mandatory maximum consumption ceilings and to prohibit the use of drinking water for cooling in waterstressed regions.

Meanwhile, the expansion of AI is exponentially increasing the water footprint due to the high thermal density of new chips. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following three questions: 1.
Does it intend to introduce binding maximum water consumption limits (WUE ceilings) for data centres, going beyond the phase of simply monitoring and reporting?
Is it considering banning the use of drinking water for cooling new facilities, obliging operators in vulnerable areas to use only dry, immersion cooling or industrial waste water technologies?

How will it review the European sustainability rating scheme to introduce restrictive criteria tailored to the specific water impact of new infrastructure dedicated exclusively to artificial intelligence?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.8.2026) The Commission, based on the Energy Efficiency Directive1, will introduce a rating scheme for data centres2, in the form of a label showcasing the energy efficiency and sustainability performance of facilities.

With the Electrification Action Plan3, the Commission announced to introduce minimum performance standards for data centres4, to ensure that new or retrofitted facilities meet sustainability criteria, including on water consumption.

In this framework, it should be recalled that the Water Framework Directive5 requires Member States to protect and, where necessary, restore water bodies to reach good status, and prevent deterioration. Replying to the specific questions of the Honourable Member: 1.

At this stage, the Commission cannot prejudge whether minimum performance standards for data centres, would take the form of binding maximum water-use ceilings. 2. As regards the use of drinking water, the Commission recognises that water stress varies significantly across regions.

The forthcoming rating scheme (label) is intended to provide easily comparable information on freshwater consumption, while allowing competent local and regional authorities to set context-specific requirements or thresholds considering local water availability and use. 3.

The Commission intends to propose an early review clause for the features of the data centre label to ensure that implementation results, and environmental, technological and market developments can be reflected, if necessary.
1 Directive (EU) 2023/1791 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on energy

efficiency and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/955 (recast): http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/1791/oj. 2 https://energy.ec.europa.eu/news/rating-scheme-data-centres-eu-commission-launches-call-feedback-2026-0327_en. 3 COM/2026/595 final: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52026DC0595 4 https://energy.ec.europa.
